questions.question_text:
The tangent line to the graph of $y=f(x)$ at the point $(2, 7)$ passes through $(0, 1)$.
What is the value of $f'(2)$?

options.why: Confused the $y$-coordinate of the point of contact with the gradient of the tangent.
Divided 7 by 2 instead of calculating the gradient $\frac{7-1}{2-0}$.
Computed the rise $7-1=6$ but forgot to divide by the run $2-0=2$.

questions.question_text:
The graph shows a curve and its tangent at $P$. What is $f'(3)$?
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.65cm,y=0.4cm]\draw[->] (0,0)--(6,0) node[right] {$x$};\draw[->] (0,0)--(0,10) node[above] {$y$};\draw[blue,thick,domain=1:5,samples=50] plot (\x,{0.3*(\x-3)^2-2*\x+9});\draw[orange,thick] (0.5,8)--(4.5,0);\fill (3,3) circle (2pt) node[above right] {$P(3,3)$};\fill (1,7) circle (2pt) node[above right,xshift=12pt,yshift=24pt] {$(1,7)$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]

options.why: Omitted the negative sign from the gradient of the decreasing tangent.
Calculated only the change in height, $3-7=-4$, without dividing by the run $3-1=2$.
Used the height of the point of contact instead of the tangent gradient.

questions.question_text: What is the primary geometric distinction between a secant line and a tangent line to a curve?

options.text: A secant line joins two distinct points on the curve; a tangent line has the same local gradient as the curve at the point of contact.
A secant line touches at one point (instantaneous rate of change); a tangent line passes through two points (average rate of change).
options.why: Inverted the definitions of a secant line and a tangent line.

options.text: A secant line is curved; a tangent line is a straight line.
options.why: Both secant lines and tangent lines are straight lines.

options.text: A secant line only exists for linear functions; a tangent line only exists for curves.
options.why: Secants and tangents are defined for non-linear functions.

questions.solution_text: A secant joins two distinct points and gives the average rate of change. A tangent has the same local gradient as the curve at the point of contact and gives the instantaneous rate of change.

questions.question_text: Over the interval $[a, b]$, what does the difference quotient $\dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$ calculate?

options.text: The gradient of the secant line, giving the average rate of change over $[a, b]$.
The exact instantaneous rate of change at the midpoint of $[a, b]$.
options.why: The difference quotient gives the average rate over the interval, which may not match the instantaneous rate at the midpoint.

options.text: The gradient of the tangent line at $x=b$.
options.why: The tangent gradient at $x=b$ is a limit as $a\to b$, not the secant over a non-zero interval.

options.text: The total change in $y$ over the interval.
options.why: The total change in $y$ is $f(b)-f(a)$; dividing by $b-a$ gives the rate of change.

questions.solution_text: $\dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$ is the gradient of the secant line over $[a, b]$.

questions.question_text: A secant joins $P(3,f(3))$ and $Q(3+h,f(3+h))$, where $h\ne0$. Which expression gives its gradient?

options.why: Added the two heights instead of finding their difference.
Used the second point's horizontal coordinate instead of the horizontal change $(3+h)-3=h$.
Reversed rise and run; gradient is rise divided by run.

questions.question_text:
The graph shows a curve and its tangent at $P$. What is $f'(2)$?
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.7cm,y=0.5cm]\draw[->] (0,0)--(5,0) node[right] {$x$};\draw[->] (0,0)--(0,7) node[above] {$y$};\draw[blue,thick,domain=0:4,samples=50] plot (\x,{0.5*(\x-2)^2+3});\draw[orange,thick] (0,3)--(4.5,3);\fill (2,3) circle (2pt) node[below] {$P(2,3)$};\fill (4,3) circle (2pt) node[below] {$(4,3)$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]

options.why: Used the height of the point of contact instead of the tangent gradient.
Used the horizontal change $4-2=2$ instead of dividing the rise by the run.
Confused a horizontal tangent, whose gradient is zero, with a vertical line.

questions.question_text:
The graph shows a curve and its tangent at $P$. What is $f'(2)$?
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.65cm,y=0.45cm]\draw[->] (0,0)--(6,0) node[right] {$x$};\draw[->] (0,0)--(0,9) node[above] {$y$};\draw[blue,thick,domain=0.5:4.5,samples=50] plot (\x,{0.3*(\x-2)^2+1.5*\x-1});\draw[orange,thick] (0.7,0.05)--(5,6.5);\fill (2,2) circle (2pt) node[below right] {$P(2,2)$};\fill (4,5) circle (2pt) node[below right] {$(4,5)$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]

options.why: Calculated the rise $5-2=3$ without dividing by the run $4-2=2$.
Reversed the order of subtraction for the heights but not for the horizontal coordinates.
Divided the coordinates of $(4,5)$ to get $5/4$, incorrectly treating the tangent as passing through the origin.

questions.question_text:
The graph shows a curve and its tangent at $P$. What is $f'(1.5)$?
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.75cm,y=0.45cm]\draw[->] (-2,0)--(4,0) node[right] {$x$};\draw[->] (0,-5)--(0,5) node[above] {$y$};\draw[blue,thick,domain=-0.5:3,samples=50] plot (\x,{0.3*(\x-1.5)^2+2.4*\x-1.85});\draw[orange,thick] (-1.2,-4.73)--(2.8,4.87);\fill (1.5,1.75) circle (2pt) node[below right] {$P(1.5,1.75)$};\fill (-1,-4.25) circle (2pt) node[below left] {$(-1,-4.25)$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]

options.why: Calculated $1.75+(-4.25)=-2.5$ instead of the rise $1.75-(-4.25)=6$, then divided by the correct run $2.5$.
Calculated the correct rise $6$ but used $1.5+(-1)=0.5$ instead of the run $1.5-(-1)=2.5$.
Calculated only the rise $1.75-(-4.25)=6$ and omitted division by the run.
